notes: OPENROUTER is the user-selected primary only for /code-review and /ship-review in this checkout: run it with scripts/local/Invoke-OpenRouterTask.ps1, which uses Junie and defaults to z-ai/glm-5.2. It is deliberately first for those review stages despite being metered; that is a local model preference, not a general billing rule. Other commands retain their existing routes and may use other models. The remaining reserve hosts (antigravity, junie) sit between the flat-rate primary hosts and the floor. Their position below the primaries is a BILLING order, not a quality one: flat-rate subscription capacity is spent first because it is already paid for whether used or not, and metered capacity is held back. They sit ABOVE the floor because both still clear the quality bar the floor defines -- reaching for reserve beats dropping a tier. They are absent from cheap commands, where the floor costs little anyway. ORDERING BETWEEN THE TWO RESERVES: junie reaches a newer Claude generation (Opus 5, Sonnet 5) than antigravity (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, GPT-OSS 120B), but junie's budget is 10-20 credits per 30 days against antigravity's weekly allowance. Antigravity goes first because both clear the floor by construction, and spending the plentiful pool on work the scarcer one need not touch is the whole point of holding a reserve. Reach past antigravity to junie when the work genuinely wants the newer generation. ANTIGRAVITY (binary 'agy') is the Google AI Plus successor path after consumer Login-with-Google Gemini CLI was deprecated; under Plus it exposes separate Gemini Flash/Pro and Claude/GPT-OSS weekly pools. JUNIE draws JetBrains AI credits (All Products Pack -> AI Pro). On both reserves consumption is proportional to token cost, unlike the flat-rate primaries, so the tier changes spend directly. OpenRouter and the reserves are absent from agents.tiers, so their tiers resolve unpinned: the tier is advice about what to select in that tool, not a resolved model. Both expose model and effort controls, so they would populate agents.tiers cleanly if the closed host set is ever opened -- see #76. THIRD RESERVE LANE (gemini-api): Gemini CLI authenticated with a Gemini API key on Google AI Studio Free Tier. This is a separate capacity pool on top of agy and junie, not a reconfiguration of either. Free-tier reach is Flash and Flash-Lite only (Pro needs Pay-As-You-Go). Observed caps: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite 15 RPM / 250K TPM / 500 RPD; Gemini 3 / 3.5 Flash 5 RPM / 250K TPM / 20 RPD; plus a shared 1.5M tokens/day workspace quota. Tier mapping: fast = Flash Lite (500 RPD, mechanical workhorse), balanced = Flash 3.5 (20 RPD, reserve for isolated reasoning). Routed only into mechanical commands where Flash Lite clears the floor; reasoning-heavy commands (/grill-with-docs, /speckit-plan, /speckit-analyze, /implement, /code-review, /architect) stay off this lane. Free-tier prompts/responses may be used for Google product training -- keep enterprise-private work off this lane. See spike-findings.md. OPENROUTER CHEAP LANE: `openrouter` now also appears at `fast` on the mechanical commands (/task, /speckit-specify, /speckit-tasks, /gherkin), below the free gemini-api lane and above the flat-rate floor. That placement deliberately inverts the billing order the other reserves follow. Invoke-OpenRouterTask.ps1 resolves `fast` to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash at $0.077/$0.154 per 1M tokens, so a mechanical run costs cents, while the flat-rate floor draws on the same weekly Claude/Cursor allowance that /implement and /speckit-plan compete for. Paying cents to keep scarce judgment capacity for the stages that need it is the trade this lane exists to make -- it is the one place in the map where metered capacity is spent ahead of flat-rate, and it is spent because it is nearly free, not because it is better. The lane stays off the reasoning-heavy commands and off /refactor for the same reason gemini-api does: those are the rows where a shallow model's miss is silent. TRUST LEVELS, expressed through the launcher's tiers: fast = deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, the cheap mechanical writer; balanced = deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, stronger cheap work; deep = z-ai/glm-5.2, the judgment baseline and the tier /code-review already uses. Scout/draft-only models such as cohere/north-mini-code:free are never routed -- reach for them with -Model when drafting, and verify the result with a routed lane before trusting a write. See docs/adr/0010-cheap-metered-lane-precedes-the-flat-rate-floor.md for the argument behind the placement and the alternatives rejected.

/task.why: Reading an issue and naming a branch is deterministic script execution; no reasoning tier does this better than another.

/grill-with-docs.why: Interrogating a plan for hidden assumptions and coining precise glossary terms is the judgment work that separates tiers; a shallow model produces a shallow grill and the miss is silent.

/speckit-specify.why: Converts an already-settled brief into spec sections; mostly structured transcription once the grill has done the thinking.

/speckit-clarify.why: Surfaces remaining ambiguity as direct questions against a spec that already exists; recognizing a gap is easier than authoring the resolution.

/speckit-plan.why: Architectural reasoning about how a feature gets built; a wrong plan compounds through every later stage, so this is where a silent miss costs the most.

/speckit-tasks.why: Decomposes an approved plan into a task list; largely mechanical once the plan states the shape of the work.

/speckit-analyze.why: Cross-checks spec, plan, tasks, and the constitution for contradictions; catching a subtle inconsistency is exactly the kind of miss that stays silent on a weaker model.

/implement.why: Writes the production code and tests; the highest-token stage and the one where quality variance is most visible, so it anchors the top of the map.

/gherkin.why: Translates settled scenarios into Gherkin; opt-in stage with moderate reasoning and a small, checkable surface.

/refactor.why: Reduces complexity and duplication against numeric gate thresholds; the target is measurable, so the model mainly needs to satisfy a check it can verify itself.

/code-review.why: Three-axis diff review; the risk axis (security, concurrency, coverage gaps) needs real judgment even though standards and spec checks are closer to a checklist.

/remediate.why: Applies a frozen set of above-bar review findings; the what is already decided, but the fix is still production code whose silent miss reopens the review loop.

/architect.why: Interprets Stryker survivors and decides whether the invariant or the test is wrong; a mistaken call here either hides a real gap or adds a test that proves nothing.

/ship-review.why: Final pre-PR fan-out; high stakes for what it gates but review-only and checklist-heavy, so balanced clears it without deep's cost.

/address-pr-review.why: Adjudicating external review comments and applying only justified fixes is the same silent-miss risk as /code-review, plus a bounded production-code change; balanced is the floor because the comment set already names the work.
